levels.title: List Repeatable Low-Risk Work Tasks
levels.objective: Demonstrate list repeatable low-risk work tasks using a controlled, repeatable AI-assisted work process with appropriate checks.
levels.teaching: Good automation candidates recur frequently, have structured inputs and allow errors to be corrected. In a practical example, An office team copies approved event registrations into a weekly summary every Friday. The recommended workflow is to start with a reversible, low-risk registration summary using fictional records. Avoid: automate confidential hiring decisions without review or give an untested bot permission to delete the source spreadsheet.
levels.workedExample: An office team copies approved event registrations into a weekly summary every Friday. Action: Start with a reversible, low-risk registration summary using fictional records.
levels.commonMistake: Automate confidential hiring decisions without review
levels.remediation: Pilot scope should be bounded and recoverable.
levels.hint: Identify the option that follows this workflow principle: Good automation candidates recur frequently, have structured inputs and allow errors to be corrected.

challenges.prompt: For "List Repeatable Low-Risk Work Tasks", consider this workflow problem: An office team copies approved event registrations into a weekly summary every Friday. Which design choice fits the goal?

options.a: Start with a reversible, low-risk registration summary using fictional records
options.b: Automate confidential hiring decisions without review
options.c: Give an untested bot permission to delete the source spreadsheet

challenges.feedback: Good automation candidates recur frequently, have structured inputs and allow errors to be corrected. Best choice: Start with a reversible, low-risk registration summary using fictional records.

challenges.prompt: An automation designer is helping a small café listing repeatable stock reporting tasks. Which workflow step is safest and most testable?

challenges.feedback: Pilot a reversible weekly stock summary with defined inputs and a named reviewer. Pilot scope should be bounded and recoverable.

challenges.prompt: Evaluate this workflow statement for "List Repeatable Low-Risk Work Tasks": A predictable low-risk task is a better first automation pilot than an irreversible high-stakes decision.
challenges.feedback: Pilot scope should be bounded and recoverable.

levels.title: Recognize Tasks Needing Human Judgment
levels.objective: Demonstrate recognize tasks needing human judgment using a controlled, repeatable AI-assisted work process with appropriate checks.
levels.teaching: Decisions affecting rights, finances or people may require an accountable human reviewer. In a practical example, An AI workflow drafts an applicant rejection letter from incomplete interview notes. The recommended workflow is to require authorized human confirmation of the decision and reasons before sending. Avoid: allow automatic rejection based on the generated tone or hide the source notes from the person responsible.
levels.workedExample: An AI workflow drafts an applicant rejection letter from incomplete interview notes. Action: Require authorized human confirmation of the decision and reasons before sending.
levels.commonMistake: Allow automatic rejection based on the generated tone
levels.remediation: Accountability must remain with authorized people.
levels.hint: Identify the option that follows this workflow principle: Decisions affecting rights, finances or people may require an accountable human reviewer.

challenges.prompt: For "Recognize Tasks Needing Human Judgment", consider this workflow problem: An AI workflow drafts an applicant rejection letter from incomplete interview notes. Which design choice fits the goal?

options.a: Hide the source notes from the person responsible
options.b: Require authorized human confirmation of the decision and reasons before sending
options.c: Allow automatic rejection based on the generated tone

challenges.feedback: Decisions affecting rights, finances or people may require an accountable human reviewer. Best choice: Require authorized human confirmation of the decision and reasons before sending.

challenges.prompt: An automation designer is helping a hospital office summarizing a fictional appointment reschedule. Which workflow step is safest and most testable?

options.b: Prepare a nonbinding reschedule summary for an authorized person to verify before contacting patients
options.c: Automatically change appointment times for everyone without review

challenges.feedback: Prepare a nonbinding reschedule summary for an authorized person to verify before contacting patients. Accountability must remain with authorized people.

levels.title: Define a Clear Workflow Outcome
levels.objective: Demonstrate define a clear workflow outcome using a controlled, repeatable AI-assisted work process with appropriate checks.
levels.teaching: A workflow needs a trigger, intended artifact, owner and measurable acceptance condition. In a practical example, A charity wants to reduce time spent compiling volunteer shift updates. The recommended workflow is to define a weekly summary draft due Friday with accurate shift counts and a named reviewer. Avoid: ask for "more productivity" without any observable result or measure success only by number of app integrations.

levels.commonMistake: Ask for "more productivity" without any observable result
levels.remediation: Without a defined outcome, efficiency claims cannot be checked.
levels.hint: Identify the option that follows this workflow principle: A workflow needs a trigger, intended artifact, owner and measurable acceptance condition.

options.a: Ask for "more productivity" without any observable result
options.b: Measure success only by number of app integrations
options.c: Define a weekly summary draft due Friday with accurate shift counts and a named reviewer

challenges.feedback: A workflow needs a trigger, intended artifact, owner and measurable acceptance condition. Best choice: Define a weekly summary draft due Friday with accurate shift counts and a named reviewer.

levels.title: Identify Inputs and Access Requirements
levels.objective: Demonstrate identify inputs and access requirements using a controlled, repeatable AI-assisted work process with appropriate checks.
levels.teaching: List minimal required inputs and permissions before connecting a service. In a practical example, A fictional retailer wants an automation that counts weekly orders from an approved sheet. The recommended workflow is to grant read access only to order status, date and ID fields needed for counts. Avoid: give the workflow administrator access to all company files or copy customer passwords into the automation's notes.

levels.commonMistake: Give the workflow administrator access to all company files
levels.remediation: Least privilege protects unrelated information.

options.c: Copy customer passwords into the automation's notes

challenges.feedback: List minimal required inputs and permissions before connecting a service. Best choice: Grant read access only to order status, date and ID fields needed for counts.

levels.title: Estimate the Cost of a Bad Answer

levels.teaching: Error severity should determine whether a workflow can run unattended or requires review. levels.commonMistake: Transfer money automatically when a model sounds certain

levels.hint: Identify the option that follows this workflow principle: Error severity should determine whether a workflow can run unattended or requires review.

options.a: Ignore a mismatch because the invoice is formatted professionally

options.c: Transfer money automatically when a model sounds certain

levels.title: Checkpoint: Select a Safe AI Workflow
levels.objective: Demonstrate checkpoint: select a safe ai workflow using a controlled, repeatable AI-assisted work process with appropriate checks.
levels.teaching: Choose a candidate using data sensitivity, reversibility, frequency and review effort. In a practical example, A school administration office compares attendance summaries with automatic student disciplinary decisions. The recommended workflow is to pilot an aggregate attendance summary with a human check rather than automatic disciplinary action. Avoid: use an opaque model to punish students without explanation or enable bulk deletion for faster cleanup.

levels.commonMistake: Use an opaque model to punish students without explanation
levels.remediation: The first pilot should minimize harms and clarify responsibility.
levels.hint: Identify the option that follows this workflow principle: Choose a candidate using data sensitivity, reversibility, frequency and review effort.

options.a: Use an opaque model to punish students without explanation

options.c: Pilot an aggregate attendance summary with a human check rather than automatic disciplinary action

challenges.feedback: Choose a candidate using data sensitivity, reversibility, frequency and review effort. Best choice: Pilot an aggregate attendance summary with a human check rather than automatic disciplinary action.

levels.title: Write a Structured Task Brief

Avoid: ask the model to invent tasks when the sheet is empty or paste credentials into the prompt body.

levels.hint: Identify the option that follows this workflow principle: A no-code step must specify inputs, output fields, constraints and what happens on missing data.

challenges.prompt: For "Write a Structured Task Brief", consider this workflow problem: A weekly report uses a date range and a list of fictional completed tasks. Which design choice fits the goal?

options.a: Specify permitted columns, date filter, output heading and explicit missing-field behavior

options.c: Paste credentials into the prompt body

challenges.feedback: A no-code step must specify inputs, output fields, constraints and what happens on missing data. Best choice: Specify permitted columns, date filter, output heading and explicit missing-field behavior.

The recommended workflow is to separate intake validation, drafting, reviewer confirmation and email sending. levels.commonMistake: Send emails immediately from unchecked free-text fields
levels.remediation: Side effects should occur only after the required checks.
levels.hint: Identify the option that follows this workflow principle: A multi-step flow should validate intermediate outputs before side effects occur.

levels.teaching: A reproducible workflow should record where values came from and what defaults were applied. In a practical example, A forecast draft uses a fictional list of sales and a manually chosen growth rate. The recommended workflow is to store the input file name, period and explicitly labelled growth assumption alongside the draft. Avoid: present the assumed rate as an observed historical fact or discard the source references after generating the slide.
levels.workedExample: A forecast draft uses a fictional list of sales and a manually chosen growth rate. Action: Store the input file name, period and explicitly labelled growth assumption alongside the draft.
levels.commonMistake: Present the assumed rate as an observed historical fact
levels.remediation: Provenance enables reviewers to challenge the calculation.
levels.hint: Identify the option that follows this workflow principle: A reproducible workflow should record where values came from and what defaults were applied.

options.a: Store the input file name, period and explicitly labelled growth assumption alongside the draft
options.b: Present the assumed rate as an observed historical fact
options.c: Discard the source references after generating the slide

challenges.feedback: A reproducible workflow should record where values came from and what defaults were applied. Best choice: Store the input file name, period and explicitly labelled growth assumption alongside the draft.

levels.title: Escalate Sensitive or High-Stakes Decisions
levels.objective: Demonstrate escalate sensitive or high-stakes decisions using a controlled, repeatable AI-assisted work process with appropriate checks.
levels.teaching: An automated step must stop and request authorized review when risk thresholds are met. In a practical example, A no-code system detects conflicting bank details on a supplier invoice. The recommended workflow is to pause the workflow and request independent authorized verification. Avoid: send the payment because the amount is small or overwrite the old account without preserving the change history.
levels.workedExample: A no-code system detects conflicting bank details on a supplier invoice. Action: Pause the workflow and request independent authorized verification.
levels.commonMistake: Send the payment because the amount is small
levels.remediation: Human escalation is a feature, not a failure.
levels.hint: Identify the option that follows this workflow principle: An automated step must stop and request authorized review when risk thresholds are met.

challenges.prompt: For "Escalate Sensitive or High-Stakes Decisions", consider this workflow problem: A no-code system detects conflicting bank details on a supplier invoice. Which design choice fits the goal?

options.a: Overwrite the old account without preserving the change history
options.b: Pause the workflow and request independent authorized verification
options.c: Send the payment because the amount is small

challenges.feedback: An automated step must stop and request authorized review when risk thresholds are met. Best choice: Pause the workflow and request independent authorized verification.

challenges.prompt: An automation designer is helping a clinic office identifying a fictional urgent reschedule request. Which workflow step is safest and most testable?

options.a: Hide the urgency indicator so the report can finish
options.b: Escalate a possible high-risk reschedule to authorized clinical staff before taking action
options.c: Allow an unreviewed system to change an urgent appointment

challenges.feedback: Escalate a possible high-risk reschedule to authorized clinical staff before taking action. Human escalation is a feature, not a failure.

challenges.prompt: Evaluate this workflow statement for "Escalate Sensitive or High-Stakes Decisions": A safe automated flow can be designed to stop when high-risk conditions appear.
challenges.feedback: Human escalation is a feature, not a failure.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Audit an AI-Generated Report
levels.objective: Demonstrate checkpoint: audit an ai-generated report using a controlled, repeatable AI-assisted work process with appropriate checks.
levels.teaching: Review source totals, unsupported statements, exposure risks and actions before publication. In a practical example, A generated management note gives 42 completed jobs while the source has 39. The recommended workflow is to reconcile IDs, correct the figure and record the discrepancy before sending. Avoid: accept the 42 because the writing is fluent or remove the original file to avoid confusion.
levels.workedExample: A generated management note gives 42 completed jobs while the source has 39. Action: Reconcile IDs, correct the figure and record the discrepancy before sending.
levels.commonMistake: Accept the 42 because the writing is fluent
levels.remediation: Automated reports require reconciliation.
levels.hint: Identify the option that follows this workflow principle: Review source totals, unsupported statements, exposure risks and actions before publication.

challenges.prompt: For "Checkpoint: Audit an AI-Generated Report", consider this workflow problem: A generated management note gives 42 completed jobs while the source has 39. Which design choice fits the goal?

options.a: Accept the 42 because the writing is fluent
options.b: Remove the original file to avoid confusion
options.c: Reconcile IDs, correct the figure and record the discrepancy before sending

challenges.feedback: Review source totals, unsupported statements, exposure risks and actions before publication. Best choice: Reconcile IDs, correct the figure and record the discrepancy before sending.

challenges.prompt: An automation designer is helping a nonprofit checking a generated donor-free activity report. Which workflow step is safest and most testable?

levels.title: Map Human Review Checkpoints
levels.objective: Demonstrate map human review checkpoints using a controlled, repeatable AI-assisted work process with appropriate checks.
levels.teaching: Review gates should be placed before irreversible actions, not only after output delivery. In a practical example, A social publishing automation drafts posts from approved product details. The recommended workflow is to require an editor to check claims and approve the exact version before scheduling. Avoid: automatically publish the draft then ask for a review or use an unrecorded verbal approval as the only audit evidence.
levels.workedExample: A social publishing automation drafts posts from approved product details. Action: Require an editor to check claims and approve the exact version before scheduling.
levels.commonMistake: Automatically publish the draft then ask for a review
levels.remediation: Approval must occur before side effects.
levels.hint: Identify the option that follows this workflow principle: Review gates should be placed before irreversible actions, not only after output delivery.

challenges.prompt: For "Map Human Review Checkpoints", consider this workflow problem: A social publishing automation drafts posts from approved product details. Which design choice fits the goal?

options.a: Require an editor to check claims and approve the exact version before scheduling
options.b: Automatically publish the draft then ask for a review
options.c: Use an unrecorded verbal approval as the only audit evidence

challenges.feedback: Review gates should be placed before irreversible actions, not only after output delivery. Best choice: Require an editor to check claims and approve the exact version before scheduling.

challenges.prompt: An automation designer is helping an HR team drafting but not sending interview scheduling emails. Which workflow step is safest and most testable?

options.a: Send every generated invitation as soon as its draft exists
options.b: Allow the model to change a candidate's interview date without confirmation
options.c: Draft candidate emails but require an authorized HR reviewer to approve each exact message before sending

challenges.feedback: Draft candidate emails but require an authorized HR reviewer to approve each exact message before sending. Approval must occur before side effects.

challenges.feedback: Approval must occur before side effects.

levels.title: Define Repeatable Inputs and Outputs
levels.objective: Demonstrate define repeatable inputs and outputs using a controlled, repeatable AI-assisted work process with appropriate checks.
levels.teaching: Specify triggers, transformations, structured payloads and destination fields for repeatability. In a practical example, A weekly order report reads completed order records each Monday. The recommended workflow is to define the Monday schedule, date window, required fields, CSV output and exception handling. Avoid: let the time window vary unpredictably each run or mix customer notes into a public dashboard without permission.
levels.workedExample: A weekly order report reads completed order records each Monday. Action: Define the Monday schedule, date window, required fields, CSV output and exception handling.
levels.commonMistake: Let the time window vary unpredictably each run
levels.remediation: Determinism helps diagnose failures and drift.
levels.hint: Identify the option that follows this workflow principle: Specify triggers, transformations, structured payloads and destination fields for repeatability.

challenges.prompt: For "Define Repeatable Inputs and Outputs", consider this workflow problem: A weekly order report reads completed order records each Monday. Which design choice fits the goal?

options.a: Mix customer notes into a public dashboard without permission
options.b: Define the Monday schedule, date window, required fields, CSV output and exception handling
options.c: Let the time window vary unpredictably each run

challenges.feedback: Specify triggers, transformations, structured payloads and destination fields for repeatability. Best choice: Define the Monday schedule, date window, required fields, CSV output and exception handling.

challenges.prompt: An automation designer is helping a warehouse automation summarizing fictional receipts. Which workflow step is safest and most testable?

options.c: Infer missing invoice totals from other rows

levels.commonMistake: Approve when the generated text sounds persuasive
levels.remediation: Risk-focused checks catch recurring defects.
levels.hint: Identify the option that follows this workflow principle: Quality checks should be observable and tied to likely failure modes of the actual automation.

options.a: Approve when the generated text sounds persuasive
options.b: Use only a cosmetic spelling check
options.c: Check input count, missing-owner exceptions, status values and approved recipient list

challenges.feedback: Quality checks should be observable and tied to likely failure modes of the actual automation. Best choice: Check input count, missing-owner exceptions, status values and approved recipient list.

levels.title: Test a Workflow on Fictional Data
levels.objective: Demonstrate test a workflow on fictional data using a controlled, repeatable AI-assisted work process with appropriate checks.
levels.teaching: Synthetic cases should cover normal runs, missing fields, duplicates and trigger retries. In a practical example, A form-to-sheet workflow sometimes runs twice for the same submission. The recommended workflow is to test duplicate delivery and use a stable event ID to avoid adding the same row twice. Avoid: use real confidential submissions for initial debugging or assume the connector never retries an event.
levels.workedExample: A form-to-sheet workflow sometimes runs twice for the same submission. Action: Test duplicate delivery and use a stable event ID to avoid adding the same row twice.
levels.commonMistake: Use real confidential submissions for initial debugging
levels.remediation: Retry-safe logic keeps a single business event from duplicating actions.
levels.hint: Identify the option that follows this workflow principle: Synthetic cases should cover normal runs, missing fields, duplicates and trigger retries.

challenges.prompt: For "Test a Workflow on Fictional Data", consider this workflow problem: A form-to-sheet workflow sometimes runs twice for the same submission. Which design choice fits the goal?

options.a: Test duplicate delivery and use a stable event ID to avoid adding the same row twice
options.b: Use real confidential submissions for initial debugging
options.c: Assume the connector never retries an event

challenges.feedback: Synthetic cases should cover normal runs, missing fields, duplicates and trigger retries. Best choice: Test duplicate delivery and use a stable event ID to avoid adding the same row twice.

challenges.prompt: An automation designer is helping an event coordinator building a no-code registration system. Which workflow step is safest and most testable?

options.a: Append a new record every time the same webhook retries
options.b: Use real attendees' full private details in initial public tests
options.c: Use stable registration event IDs and test normal, duplicate, invalid and retried submissions

challenges.feedback: Use stable registration event IDs and test normal, duplicate, invalid and retried submissions. Retry-safe logic keeps a single business event from duplicating actions.

challenges.feedback: Retry-safe logic keeps a single business event from duplicating actions.

levels.title: Measure Corrections and Time Saved
levels.objective: Demonstrate measure corrections and time saved using a controlled, repeatable AI-assisted work process with appropriate checks.
levels.teaching: Compare automation work against a defined manual baseline and record rework. In a practical example, A monthly report formerly took 90 minutes and now takes 35 minutes plus 20 minutes review. The recommended workflow is to report net time saved as 35 minutes and note corrected errors. Avoid: claim 90 minutes saved because generation is instantaneous or ignore review time when assessing efficiency.
levels.workedExample: A monthly report formerly took 90 minutes and now takes 35 minutes plus 20 minutes review. Action: Report net time saved as 35 minutes and note corrected errors.
levels.commonMistake: Claim 90 minutes saved because generation is instantaneous
levels.remediation: Net savings = prior manual time minus automated handling and human review time.
levels.hint: Identify the option that follows this workflow principle: Compare automation work against a defined manual baseline and record rework.

challenges.prompt: For "Measure Corrections and Time Saved", consider this workflow problem: A monthly report formerly took 90 minutes and now takes 35 minutes plus 20 minutes review. Which design choice fits the goal?

options.a: Ignore review time when assessing efficiency
options.b: Report net time saved as 35 minutes and note corrected errors
options.c: Claim 90 minutes saved because generation is instantaneous

challenges.feedback: Compare automation work against a defined manual baseline and record rework. Best choice: Report net time saved as 35 minutes and note corrected errors.

challenges.prompt: An automation designer is helping a small office measuring a supervised AI-assisted weekly process. Which workflow step is safest and most testable?

options.a: Ignore the cost of fixing errors when measuring benefit
options.b: Compare the old manual time with automation, supervision and correction time using the same workload
options.c: Claim the full previous work time as saved without subtracting review

challenges.feedback: Compare the old manual time with automation, supervision and correction time using the same workload. Net savings = prior manual time minus automated handling and human review time.
